level1_summaries.content: Stereotypical motor movements (SMMs) are common in individuals with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and are characterized by repetitive, rhythmical, and seemingly purposeless actions. visual_elements.content: Figure 2A shows a precision-recall curve for the first analysis of the algorithm using the initially annotated 755 SMMs in the test data. The x-axis represents recall, and the y-axis represents precision. There are three curves plotted: one for female participants (blue), one for male participants (orange), and one for all participants (gray). The curves show a general trend of decreasing precision as recall increases. Figure 2B displays a precision-recall curve for the second analysis after the reannotation process. The x-axis represents recall, and the y-axis represents precision. Two curves are shown: one for the initial annotation (red), and one for the reannotation (green). The reannotation curve generally shows higher precision values for a given recall value compared to the initial annotation curve, indicating improved accuracy after the reannotation process.

The figure displays two scatter plots comparing the algorithm's performance to manual annotation in quantifying Stereotypical Motor Movements (SMMs). Panel A shows the correlation between the algorithm and manual annotation in terms of SMMs per minute, with the x-axis representing manual annotation (%) and the y-axis representing the algorithm's output (%). The data points cluster around a dotted line indicating perfect agreement, with a correlation coefficient (r) of 0.80, a p-value less than 0.001, and NRMSE of 0.27. Panel B shows the correlation in terms of the percentage of time with SMMs, with a similar structure of axes. Here, the correlation coefficient is 0.88, the p-value is less than 0.001, and the NRMSE is 0.19.
